name: Kasa Smart Dimmer KS220 (US)

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only. TP-Link lists Bluetooth 4.2 for setup only.

matter.note: TP-Link's Matter dimmer is the separate KS225; the KS220 pages we saw make no Matter claim. KS220 is still sold alongside it, so we used it.

apple_home.note: TP-Link lists Apple Home as a third-party platform. The user guide covers adding it in the Home app with its HomeKit code; a home hub (HomePod or Apple TV) is optional, for remote access.

google_home.note: Listed by TP-Link as a supported third-party platform.

alexa.note: Listed by TP-Link as a supported third-party platform.

smartthings.note: Listed by TP-Link as a supported third-party platform.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's TP-Link Smart Home integration lists the KS220 as a supported wall switch.

hubRequired.note: Connects straight to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi; TP-Link's datasheet title says no hub required.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's TP-Link integration talks to the switch directly on your network, not through TP-Link's cloud. HomeKit control also runs on the local network; TP-Link's guide says a home hub is only optional.

switchForm.note: Replaces a standard wall switch and comes with a wall plate.

dimmer.note: TRIAC dimming; 300 W incandescent/halogen, 150 W LED.

gangs.note: TP-Link's datasheet says it doesn't work with 3-way (multi-location) wiring.

summary: The Kasa KS220 is a Wi-Fi dimmer that replaces a standard US wall switch and needs a neutral wire. TP-Link lists Apple Home (through HomeKit), Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings, and Home Assistant supports it in its TP-Link integration. No hub is needed. It handles 150 W of LED or 300 W of incandescent, on single-pole circuits only.
caveats: Needs a neutral wire and does not support 3-way wiring.
Not a Matter device; TP-Link's Matter dimmer is the KS225.
LED loads are capped at 150 W.
